page: Microsoft Azure D96pds_v6 is a general-purpose server instance powered by the ARM64 architecture. It features 96 dedicated physical cores utilizing the Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz. The CPU allocation is dedicated with one thread per core, supported by 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 128 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Additionally, it includes 5669 GB of local storage and is premium storage capable, with no integrated GPU.

In benchmark evaluations, the D96pds_v6 demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test, Geekbench multi-core score, and software compilation with Clang all place in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory performance is also highly competitive, with both small-block and large-block read-only memory bandwidth reaching top-tier status. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput also rank in the top 10%, indicating highly efficient data processing capabilities. Conversely, single-core performance metrics, such as Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core, fall into the average tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM-based Neoverse-N2 architecture delivers high multi-threaded resource density and memory bandwidth without the premium associated with traditional x86 architectures. The combination of 96 dedicated physical cores, 384 GB of RAM, and over 5.6 TB of local storage makes this instance highly suitable for multi-threaded workloads. Recommended applications include high-throughput database operations, Redis caching layers, static web serving at scale, software compilation pipelines, and multi-threaded data decompression tasks.
description: The Microsoft Azure D96pds_v6 is an ARM64-based general-purpose server instance featuring 96 dedicated physical cores powered by the Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz. It is configured with 384.0 GB of system memory and 5669 GB of local storage, with no GPU. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance delivers top-tier multi-core CPU performance, exceptional memory bandwidth, and superior database throughput, as evidenced by its top 10% rankings in multi-threaded benchmarks, Redis SET operations, and static web serving. While single-core performance remains average, the high resource density of dedicated ARM cores provides excellent qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized workloads. This server is optimized for large-scale databases, Redis caching, high-throughput web serving, and concurrent software compilation.
